"To write the text in the wanted place, you need to focus the text field first by clicking on it.
Please note that depending on the application, you might need to wait a little bit after clicking, or the text will be written too early.
This might also not be working applications that don't support standard text writing, so always test your action first!"
Click on the blue button as fast as possible

"Welcome to your first tutorial!
Here, you will try to beat the high score of a game with the help of Klick'r.
First, start the game and try to win by yourself."

"Your Condition image is now recorded!
There is now several adjustments that can be made to it, but the default settings suits our basic use case. As our target is not moving, it will only detect at the capture position, which is faster than detecting on the whole screen.
Click on the save button to register it and return to the Conditions list."
Close the Conditions list to return to the Event configuration.

"With this Condition, the scenario knows when to trigger the Actions.
You now need to define what Actions to trigger, so for this game, a click on the blue character.
Click on the Actions field to display the Actions list."

"An Action is something that is executed once the Conditions of its Event are fulfilled.
It can be a click, a swipe, a pause, an Intent (an interaction with another application) or a change in the Scenario execution, and multiple Actions can be defined for the same Event.
Click on the create Action button to create your first Action."

"First, we need to pick a type for your Action.
For this game, we simply need to click on the blue character, so choose Click to create a new Click Action."

"A Click Action is defined by a position and a press duration.
As we want to click as quickly as possible, we can keep the default press duration of 1ms, which is the lowest possible value. So we only need to define a position.
Click on the position picker button to select the Click Action position."

"You need to select the exact position to be clicked, so you need to start the game again to display the blue character, and then select its position.
Once the position is correct, click on the validate button to save it."

"The click is now correctly configured!
Click on the save button to register it and return to the Actions list."
Close the Actions list to return to the Event configuration.

"Your Event now have a Condition and an Action, which means it knows what to execute and when to execute it.
Click on the save button to register it and return to the Scenario dialog."

"The only requirement for a Scenario is to have at least one Event. As our Event already cover how to win the game, we don't need anything else.
Click on the save button the save the Scenario in database and close the configuration dialogs."

"As you can see, the play button is now available, meaning that your Scenario is valid and can be used for detection
Click on it to start the detection."

"It's playing but nothing happens?
That's normal, it will click only when the blue character is visible, remember? While keeping the scenario running, press the start game button and just watch as Klick'r will beat it for you!"

"Congratulations!
You now know the basics of Klick'r, but not all use cases will be as simple as this game. Take a look at the next tutorial to learn how to track a moving target"

"Difficult, isn't it? Let's use Klick'r to beat it !
Click on the scenario configuration icon to start editing your new scenario."

"A Scenario is the root structure of Klick'r automation.
It contains the general detection settings and a list of Events describing what will be executed when running your Scenario.
Click on the create event button to create your first event."

"An Event describe what Actions (click, swipe…) to execute when certain Conditions are met.
You must create at least one Condition and one Action in order to create a valid Event and use it in your scenario
Click on the Conditions field to display the Conditions list."

"A Condition is a part of a screenshot that will be compared to each screen frame of your device.
To beat the game, we want to click on the blue character when it's visible, so we need a Condition that is fulfilled when the character is shown on your device screen.
Click on the create Condition button to create your first Condition."

"The first step of a Condition creation is to take a screenshot for it.
As we want to click when the blue character is visible, the screenshot must contains it. Start the game again in order to display it, and then take the screenshot."
Once the screenshot is taken, you can crop it in order to only get the part that is interesting for the detection.

"For this game, the interesting part is the blue character, so crop your screenshot to only get him.
You can pinch on the screenshot to zoom on it and get a better accuracy for the crop selector."
"You can't interact with the game while the position selector is visible, but you can use this button to show and hide it, allowing you to remove that restriction at will."
Use the capture button in the floating menu to take the screenshot.
If your screenshot does not contains the blue character, you can press this button to take a new one.
Ensure the character is complete in the selector. Also try to crop it as close as possible to him in order to ease the image detection.
Click on the moving blue button as fast as possible

"Let's complicate the game a little bit more. Now, the target is randomly moving.
First, start the game and check if you can win by yourself."

"Your Condition image is now updated!
In this state, the scenario will now execute a click every time the blue character is visible anywhere on the screen, but this click will be at the same position, the one selected during the previous tutorial. So, we need to update our Action.
Click on the Actions field to display the Actions list."

"We still want to execute a single click, but this time, we want to click on the Condition and not a fixed position.
As this is still one click, we still need only one Action, so let's edit your previous click.
Click on your Action to start editing it."

"Currently, the Click Action \"Click on\" is set to \"Selected position\", meaning you have to manually set the position to be clicked. The other choice is \"Condition\", meaning the Action will click on a detected Condition coordinates.
That`s exactly what we need to beat the game. Every time the blue character will be detected, this Action will click on it.
Select it to use it in your Action."
"Click on the Condition selector option to select which detected condition to click on. We need to specify it because we can have multiple Conditions in our Event."

"For our use case it is easy, we only have one condition, the blue character.
Select it to click on this Condition when it is detected on your screen."

"That's it! Your Click Action is now correctly configured to beat the game.
Click on the save button to register it and return to the Actions list."
Close the Actions list to return to the Event configuration.

"You have updated the Condition and your Action, there is nothing more to do.
Click on the save button to register it and return to the Scenario dialog."
One last save to register your new changes in the database and close the configuration dialogs.

"Your Scenario is now configured to beat this new tutorial.
Start the detection with the floating menu play button and then, start the game."

"Congratulations!
You now know how to track a still or moving single target, but there is a lot more to learn!."

"Once again, it seems impossible to win manually, so let's use Smart AutoClicker.
Your scenario for the previous tutorial have been kept and load for this tutorial, but we will need to change a few parameters in order to win this new game.
Click on the Scenario configuration icon to start updating your new scenario."

"We still want to click on the blue character, meaning that we still only need one Condition and one Action, so only one Event.
As the use case is pretty similar to the previous game, we will keep our Event and simply update it.
Click on your previously created event to edit it."

"In a first time, we will update the Condition that detect the blue character.
Click on the Conditions field to display the Conditions list."

"As in the previous tutorial, we need to detect the blue character, but now it is moving.
Our previous Condition is already detecting the blue character, but only at one position. So you don't need to take a new screenshot, as your previous Condition already has it, we just need to change its parameters.
Click on your Condition to start editing it."

"Currently, the Condition detection type is set to \"Exact\", meaning it will only be verified at its capture position.
To win this game, we need verify the same Condition, but on the whole screen.
Select the \"Whole screen\" type to detect the blue character anywhere on the screen."

"That's it! We only needed to change the detection type in order for your Condition to suits our needs.
Click on the save button to register it and return to the Conditions list."
Close the Conditions list to return to the Event configuration.
Detecting on the whole screen takes more time that the exact position, keep that in mind when your Scenario execution timing is important.
Click on the blue button only when the red button is visible

"Let's change the rules of the game again. The blue target has stopped moving, but now it should only be clicked when the red target is visible.
First, start the game and check if you can win by yourself."

"Your Condition image is now recorded!
As the red target isn't moving, we can keep the default configuration. Click on the save button to register it and return to the Conditions list."
Close the Conditions list to return to the Event configuration.

"We now have two Conditions, one for each targets, and the Actions will be executed only if both are detected.
Click on the Actions field to display the Action list for our Event."

"The action is already set to click on the blue character, and it will only be executed when the blue and the red characters are visible together.
This is exactly the behaviour we need to beat the game, so no need to edit our click Action.
Close the Actions list to return to the Event configuration."
Click on the save button to save your Event.
"All changes must be saved in your scenario in order to be registered. Click on the save button to save your changes."

"We are ready to win this game!
Click on the start button to start the detection and then, start the game."

"Congratulations!
You now know how to combine multiple Conditions for an Event, but there is a lot more to learn!"

"Once again, it seems impossible to win manually, so let's use Smart AutoClicker.
Your scenario for the previous tutorial have been kept and load for this tutorial, but we will need to change a few parameters in order to win this new game.
Click on the Scenario configuration icon to start updating your new scenario."

"We still want to click on the blue target, but only when red on is visible. So we need to add a condition for this red target in our Event.
Click on your previously created event to edit it."

"We will combine several conditions, so we need to check the Condition operator for this event.
The Condition operator indicates how multiples conditions will be interpreted together. 'One' means only one of the Conditions for this Event must be fulfilled in order to execute the Actions.
'All' means all Conditions for this Event must be fulfilled in order to execute the Actions.
As we want to detect if two things are displayed together, we will use 'All'"

"Now we need to update our Conditions.
Click on the Conditions field to display the Conditions list."

"The previous Condition of detecting the blue target is still correct, but we need a new one for the red target.
Click on the create Condition button to create a new Condition for it."
Just like for the blue target, start the game in order to show the red target. Once it is visible, take a screenshot of it!
Is your screenshot containing the red target? You can crop it in order to only get the part that is interesting for the detection, the red target.
Use the capture button in the floating menu to take the screenshot.
If your screenshot does not contains the red target, you can press this button to take a new one.

"If your scenario is clicking too quickly, it can block you from using Klick'r menu to stop it.
In that case, you can press the physical \"Volume Down\" button of your device to stop the running scenario."
